x.d: Developed by Palestinian farmers near Jaffa in Ottoman Palestine as a mutation of the Baladi orange from about the 1840s; practically seedless, sweet, oval, thick easy-peel skin that suits export but yields little juice.
x.dt: oval · thick skin · few seeds · poor juice, stores well

v.d: Fruit carrying the Jaffa label first marketed in 1870

x.d: Small, juicy early-season juice orange found in Florida in 1879 that replaced the older Parson Brown.
Mandarin that originated in Morocco (Afourer), with deep orange easy-peel skin, sweet-tart juicy segments, typically seedless when isolated.
x.dt: deep orange, easy-peel · sweet-tart · seedless in isolation

notes: Hamlin year/behaviour from the Valencia orange article; Nadorcott from Specialty Produce (breeder wording differs between sources, so no breeder named); Tango (disputed origin) not added.
